name: Breitbart News

summary.text: Breitbart News is a conservative news and opinion website founded by Andrew Breitbart. Media Matters reports that the Mercer family invested in the site in 2011, securing a board seat for Steve Bannon, who became executive chairman after Breitbart's death in 2012 and left in January 2018. Robert Mercer said in November 2017 that he was selling his stake to his daughters.

facts.claim: Media Matters reported that Steve Bannon introduced the Mercers to Andrew Breitbart, that the Mercers' 2011 investment secured Bannon a board seat, and that Bannon served as executive chairman of Breitbart News from 2012 to 2016.
facts.quote: Bannon introduced the Mercers to Andrew Breitbart, and the Mercers' investment secured him a board seat

sources.title: Breitbart Is Not Independent, It's The Communications Arm Of The Mercers' Empire

facts.claim: Robert Mercer said in November 2017 that he was selling his stake in Breitbart News to his daughters, citing personal reasons and disagreements connected to Milo Yiannopoulos; Mediaite described the stake as originally $11 million.

sources.title: Robert Mercer Sells Stake in Breitbart Citing Disagreements with Bannon and Milo

facts.claim: Bannon left Breitbart News in January 2018 after a public falling-out over comments attributed to him in a book about Trump, the Associated Press reported; he had continued to chair editorial meetings until then.

openQuestions: The reported terms of the 2011 investment (nearly 50% for $10 million, per The New York Times) were not confirmed from the original article; Mediaite gives $11 million.
Bannon's exact chairmanship dates differ between sources (2012-2016 per Media Matters; he left the site in January 2018 per AP).
